Raw wastewater is pumped from the collection system to the headworks where it is screened and degritted.
Screened wastewater is aerobically treated in the West Aeration Basin and East Aeration Basin...designed to provide aerobic and anoxic zones to achieve nitrification and denitrification.
A 120-foot diameter secondary clarifier was constructed...Effluent from the aeration ponds is conveyed to the newly constructed 120-foot diameter secondary clarifier.
The existing 90-foot secondary clarifier will be used in parallel or serve as a backup when the 120-foot clarifier is out of service for maintenance.
The filter system consists of four pile cloth-media type filters with a nominal pore size of ten microns to remove suspended solids that would inhibit the efficiency of UV disinfection.
The pumps used for filtration are housed in a low-lift pump station.
Cloth media filters and a ultraviolet light (UV) disinfection system were installed...The UV disinfection system consists of two open channels...
Disinfected effluent is discharged to eleven rapid infiltration ponds (Ponds 1, 2, 4, 5, and 8 through 14).
The Discharger states that rapid infiltration Ponds 3, 6, and 7 are no longer used due to their close proximity to the Stanislaus River.
Sludge from the secondary clarifier was sent to an aerated above ground storage tank and stored for at least six weeks.
Both screw presses with auxiliary equipment (flocculation tanks, polymer system and sludge feed pump) were installed under a permanent canopy structure.
The sludge drying beds are uncovered and may be used in the summer for additional drying or for backup dewatering.

Decant from the sludge drying beds and screw press is pumped back to the headworks.
